title: How P&G Employees Learn, Plan and Build Financial Wellbeing
summary: Employees share how the educational resources P&G provides empowered them to gain confidence on their financial wellbeing journeys and help them reach meaningful goals.
body_markdown:
So Payton did. Around 2013, he opened an investment account and began putting away about $50 a month, an amount that felt manageable at the time.


Payton joined P&G a short time later and today is an HR leader supporting Global Business Services. Early in his P&G career, a group was hosting a Money Talks workshop focused on building wealth, and he decided to attend.


The session introduced him to new ideas about investing, including the importance of diversification. For Payton, it was another step in learning how to build financial wellbeing for the long term.


As his career and income grew, Payton continued to increase the amount he set aside as he was able. Over time, a small first step became a consistent habit of investing for his future.


But Payton doesn’t believe planning for the future means putting life on hold today. His approach at this stage is straightforward. He takes care of the essentials first, sets aside some money to enjoy life and puts much of the rest toward the future. That balance allows him to enjoy experiences like a planned trip to Japan with a friend while still staying on track with his financial goals.


His advice to others is much the same as the advice that got him started: Start with an amount that feels comfortable and make it a habit.


“The important part is starting and sticking to it,” he said. “Is that $5 or $500? The important part is starting.”


For Payton, that habit created the independence he wanted when he was younger. It also put him in a position to be there for his mother, just as she had always been there for him.


“We’re at the point where we can say, ‘Mom, you don’t have to worry about anything’,” he said. “‘You can do whatever you want to with your time now.’”


For Payton, that may be the greatest return on his investment.
